title: Subcubic weighted Gomory–Hu trees
formal: Historical question, resolved affirmatively: can an exact Gomory–Hu tree of an undirected integer-weighted graph on \(n\) vertices be constructed in truly subcubic time in \(n\), with polylogarithmic dependence on the largest capacity? The 2022 theorem gives a randomized \(\widetilde O(n^{2})\)-time construction. The 2025 theorem further gives deterministic almost-linear time in the number of edges when capacities are polynomially bounded.

source_formulation.text: Can the Gomory-Hu Tree of a weighted graph be constructed in subcubic time?
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 11

context:
Gomory and Hu proved existence of a cut-equivalent tree and constructed one using at most one fewer single-pair max-flow call than the number of vertices. Even a nearly linear individual flow routine leaves a cubic dense-graph cost in that construction.

Theorem 1.3 gives a randomized nearly quadratic algorithm for general integer-weighted graphs. The following remarks explicitly say that it does not assume an unproved near-linear max-flow algorithm. The result produces the cut tree itself.

The 2025 Theorem 1.1 obtains an \(m^{1+o(1)}\)-time deterministic construction for polynomially bounded integer weights. The capacity restriction is part of the theorem and is kept here rather than inferred away from its shorter abstract.

The original motivation contrasts all-pairs maximum flow with all-pairs shortest paths. The algorithmic upper bound for cut trees is unconditional; claiming a strict complexity separation additionally requires the relevant shortest-path hardness hypothesis.
why: A cut tree compresses all pairwise minimum cuts into one tree. Fast exact construction shows that this compact representation can also be computed efficiently, with consequences for network connectivity and comparisons between fundamental all-pairs graph problems.

sentences: The input is an undirected graph with binary-encoded integer capacities.
The output is a tree representing exact minimum-cut values and separating partitions for every vertex pair.
The 2021 source asks whether its construction can beat cubic time in the number of vertices.
A published 2022 randomized nearly quadratic algorithm answers this affirmatively.
A 2025 result further gives deterministic almost-linear time for polynomially bounded integer weights.

references.title: APMF < APSP? Gomory-Hu Tree for Unweighted Graphs in Almost-Quadratic Time
references.authors: Amir Abboud (Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel), Robert Krauthgamer (Weizmann Institute of Science, Israel), Ohad Trabelsi (University of Michigan, USA)

definitions:
The input is an explicitly represented undirected graph \(G=(V,E,w)\), with \(n\geq2\) named vertices and nonnegative integer edge capacities written in binary. Write \(W=\max(1,\max_{e\in E}w(e))\). The standard weighted representation stores at most one total capacity for each unordered vertex pair, so \(m=|E|\leq\binom n2\). Parallel edges can be combined by summing their capacities, with the time to read the original list included. Loops and zero-capacity edges do not affect cuts.

For \(S\subseteq V\), its cut capacity is
\[\delta_{G}(S)=\sum_{\{u,v\}\in E:\,|\{u,v\}\cap S|=1}w(\{u,v\}).\]
For distinct \(s,t\in V\), the minimum separating cut value is \(\lambda_{G}(s,t)=\min_{S:\,s\in S,\ t\notin S}\delta_{G}(S)\). By max-flow/min-cut duality, this is also the maximum flow value between the pair.

A Gomory–Hu tree is a weighted tree \(T\) on exactly the vertex set \(V\), with \(n-1\) edges. For every distinct pair \(s,t\), the smallest edge weight on the unique tree path from \(s\) to \(t\) must equal \(\lambda_{G}(s,t)\). In addition, removing a minimum-weight edge on that path must give a partition that is an actual minimum \(s,t\) cut of \(G\), with that capacity. Thus the output represents both cut values and cut partitions, not just a table of pairwise numbers.

The tree need not be a subgraph of \(G\), and its edge weights need not be weights of individual input edges. Capacities, cut values and tree weights are exact. A tree that approximates pairwise cuts by a multiplicative factor does not satisfy this output requirement. Disconnected components can be joined by zero-weight tree edges, so connectivity is not an essential promise.

Truly subcubic means an upper bound \(O(n^{3-\eta}\operatorname{polylog}(nW))\) for some fixed \(\eta>0\). All input reading, construction and output costs are included. In particular, for \(W=n^{O(1)}\), logarithmic factors can be absorbed into a smaller positive exponent saving. The integer-capacity regime and dependence on its representation follow the resolving work; no bound independent of the number of bits in arbitrary real weights is asserted.

The original question permits randomization. A Monte Carlo construction must output a correct exact tree with high probability on every input; failure probability refers to the algorithm's internal randomness, not a random graph distribution. A deterministic construction always gives a correct tree. The 2022 randomized guarantee already answers the historical question; derandomization is additional progress.

The notation \(\widetilde O\) in the 2022 theorem suppresses polylogarithmic factors in \(n\) and \(W\). The later deterministic bound is \(m^{1+o(1)}\) on nontrivial connected instances with polynomially bounded integer capacities, or \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) when explicitly accounting for isolated vertices and component handling. The almost-linear guarantee is not asserted here for arbitrarily large capacities.
answer_criterion: The required affirmative answer is a construction algorithm with exact cut equivalence, a uniform truly subcubic running-time bound in the specified capacity model, and its correctness guarantee. The published randomized 2022 theorem provides this. Computing only a global minimum cut, only one source’s cut values, or an approximate cut tree would not suffice.
